appraisal_events.evidence: « Mais ces pièces sont manifestement fausses, dit Bloch. » M. de Norpois ne répondit pas... Bloch ne put arriver à le faire parler de la question de la culpabilité de Dreyfus ni donner un pronostic sur le jugement.
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois pointedly leaves Bloch's direct claim unanswered and repeatedly deflects his attempts to extract a real opinion, so Bloch is denied substantive engagement while Norpois retains full control of the exchange.

appraisal_events.evidence: déclara qu'il n'approuvait pas les manifestations du Prince Henri d'Orléans... elles ne peuvent que troubler la sérénité du prétoire et encourager des agitations... qui seraient à déplorer.
appraisal_events.explanation: Norpois explicitly disapproves of the Prince's public demonstrations, folding him in with agitators of 'droite' whose actions he deplores as harmful to order.

status_effects.explanation: Bloch's direct assertion goes unanswered and his repeated probing yields nothing, leaving him without rhetorical purchase in the exchange.
Norpois maintains full discursive control, speaking at length on secondary matters while withholding any substantive answer from Bloch.
He is locally cast in a negative light as a source of deplorable agitation by Norpois's explicit disapproval.

ambiguities: Norpois's silence and evasiveness toward Bloch could be read either as calculated diplomatic prudence or as narratorial irony about his hollow authority; here it is read as a local rhetorical win for Norpois since the narration reports it as fact without undercutting cues.
